items.title: Cursor ships the Agent SDK — build and deploy custom agents as code
items.summary: An agent is now a folder: instructions.md holds the prompt, tools/ defines typed actions, skills/ holds procedures loaded on demand, mcp-connections/ adds MCP tools, channels/ wires up triggers (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket PR and CI events, Slack, webhooks, cron). CLI commands scaffold (init), run locally with a playground (dev), test with evals that assert on tool calls and reply shape (eval, github replay <pr-url> to turn a real PR into test fixtures), and ship (deploy) to Cursor-hosted infra with a URL, logs, and a dashboard for secrets.
items.why: Building a custom coding or review agent is now a scaffold-test-deploy CLI workflow with real evals, not a bespoke infra project.
items.action: Run npx @cursor/agent-sdk init with the PR-autofixer template, then agent-sdk github replay against one of your own merged PRs to see how the agent would have acted on it.

items.title: New study: when an agent fails, you can't blame the model or the harness alone
items.summary: "When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?" (arXiv, submitted Oct 23) tested 4 general-purpose harnesses (OpenCode, Codex CLI, Pi CLI, DeepAgents) against 4 models across 6 benchmarks — 111 evaluation settings, 52,168 trajectories. Harness rankings flip depending on which model they're paired with, and the pairing that scores best on task accuracy isn't always the one that completes runs validly. OpenCode ranked best on cross-model fit; DeepSeek V4 Flash Preview showed consistently high valid-completion rates across harnesses.
items.why: There's no single "best" harness design — the model you pair it with changes the ranking, so a harness that's great with one model can rank last with another.
items.action: If you're benchmarking your own harness, test it against at least two different models before trusting a single ranking from one model.
